text:
From morning until night

the goblins cry with all their might:

‘buy our fruits,

come, come and buy

quinces and apples,

lemons and oranges

plump cherries,

melons and strawberries,

rosy peaches,

wild blueberries

dark mulberries,

deep-purple blackberries,

pineapples and wild pears,

apricots and raspberries;

all reaching ripeness

together in summer;

morning arrives

and evening slips away,

buy what summer leaves:

fresh grapes from the vine,

pomegranates lovely and full,

dates and pears,

monk’s plums and greengages,

damsons too and egg plums,

come and taste them, don’t be shy:

raisins and currants,

scarlet berries,

figs in abundance

southern citrus,

sweet and fresh:

buy, stretch out your hand.’




‘Goblin Market’

translation.title: Goblin Market
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish excerpt of Christina Rossetti. The fruit catalogue, invitation, and closing source title are retained.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
